newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ABN AMRO declines forecast due high markets.
newsitem.headline: ABN AMRO declines forecast due high markets.

text.p: Dutch bank ABN AMRO NV said on Thursday that it declined to give a profit forecast for the current year because of uncertainties caused by the high level of stock markets.
Asked why the bank was not prepared to make a 1997 forecast, chairman Jan Kalff said: "The uncertainty is slightly bigger given the very high level of the stock markets."
Kalff said he was not prepared to say profits would be higher in 1997 than in 1996 although that is the widespread view among analysts.
"If I had been prepared (to say that), I would have said it in our forecast," Kalff told reporters.
"That doesn't mean we would be expecting a decrease in our profits. It's simply not possible to give any statement about the future."
Referring to current high stock market levels, Kalff said: "If that would ever turn into a fall...that would firstly have an effect on our provisions.
"It might (also) be the case that there would be an indirect effect on the general tendency of markets.
